atoms.text: When writing music, you need to include a clef. The clef defines the pitch of the notes and the pitch of the piece of music.
The clef is located at the beginning of every stave in a piece of music.
There are different clefs, and they determine the pitch the notes are played in.
Here you see the treble clef (left) and the bass clef (right). They each describe a different pitch for the notes following on the stave.
atoms.sound: Here you see the treble clef and the bass clef. They each describe a different pitch for the notes following on the stave.

feedback.end: As you can hear, the tone of the note next to the treble clef is higher than the one next to the bass clef, even though both notes are in the same position on the stave.

atoms.text: Note: The clef is very important when you are reading or writing the notes of a piece of music.
The treble clef is a commonly used clef.
atoms.sound: The treble clef is a commonly used clef.

atoms.text: The bass clef is suited for lower tones and is also very common.

atoms.a: What are the clefs used for?
b: ++To determine the pitch of a piece of music.
To protect a piece of music from thieves.

atoms.b: The two most common clefs are called the ((++treble trifle trouble)) clef and the ((brass ++bass base)) clef.
The bass clef is used in particular for ((--higher ++lower)) tones.
